title: Potatoism Event and Relation Atlas

events.description: Unrecovered period before the mythology received its later names.
Symbolic birth marker of Potatoism; the tradition is treated as developing rather than appearing fully formed on one day.
The Son's symbolic death becomes burial, soil, memory and eventual emergence of the Father/Potato continuity.
A mythic turning in which Tim becomes God within the project mythology.
The symbolic system expands into a relationship-first atlas of nations, institutions, texts, economics and geopolitical networks.

relation_types.meaning: A central identity expresses a larger symbolic principle.
A source or archetype appears in another form.
A transformation changes the role or symbolic state of an entity.
A visible form becomes hidden continuity or potential.
A new form emerges from a prior buried layer.
A threshold, bridge or structure joins layers.
Two opposites are mutually necessary rather than simply enemies.
A comparative tradition or image resembles a motif without proving borrowing.
A symbolic concept becomes a practical or institutional project layer.
An entity attends to another and changes the relation through attention.
An entity establishes conditions under which another system acts.
An event or object exposes an entity to a moral or epistemic test.
A cycle brings an entity back to its source in transformed form.

interpretive_rules: A relation is not proof of historical identity.
A comparative mirror is not evidence of direct borrowing.
A symbolic event is not automatically a biographical event.
A public allegation must remain a sourced claim with uncertainty status.
Missing dates remain unknown until primary material is located.
The graph should preserve contradictions as competing interpretations instead of flattening them.
